basis: Nonsyndromic intellectual disability affects 3/3; the supplied ancestry alone does not establish a clinical metabolic disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: carbohydrate-transport ancestry without biochemical or clinical metabolic abnormalities does not establish metabolic organ disease.

basis: Intellectual disability, skeletal malformations and cardiac defects are explicit defining features; VSD occurs in 30-79%. Coloboma and gallbladder anomalies are below 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital cardiac malformations are explicitly included in the syndrome definition, with ventricular septal defects in 30-79%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; high myopia/amblyopia and pituitary hypothyroidism each occur in 1/1 assessed. Ear positioning alone does not impair function.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: pituitary hypothyroidism represents endocrine loss of function in 1/1 assessed; the very small denominator limits confidence.
decisions.otologic: none: low-set ears are positional dysmorphism; recurrent otitis is a separate infection, without established intrinsic hearing or vestibular damage.

basis: Disabling ochronotic arthropathy defines the disease; aortic stenosis occurs in 30-79% and hearing abnormalities in 80-99% per HPO. Pigmentation alone is nondamaging; stones are separate.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: disabling axial and peripheral ochronotic arthropathy is explicitly part of the disease definition; arthritis affects 80-99%.

basis: Oral inflammation/leukoplakia affects 8/11; esophageal strictures and persistent finger deformities occur in 30-79%. Urethral stenosis affects only 4/22.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: camptodactyly is persistent finger contracture and is annotated at 30-79%; this supports locomotor involvement beyond cutaneous webbing alone.

basis: Microcephaly and renal agenesis define the syndrome. Micrognathia affects 3/3; structural limb and cardiac defects each occur in 1/3 (~33%). Very small cohort.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: micrognathia affects 3/3 and structural limb malformations occur in 1/3; skeletal disease is associated rather than a defining diagnostic axis.

basis: Refractory plasma-cell malignancies are predominantly myeloma: destructive bone lesions affect most and disease-related renal impairment about 30-50%. Treatment effects excluded.

decisions.renal: involved: myeloma dominates refractory plasma-cell malignancies; direct light-chain-related renal impairment affects approximately 30-50% over the course.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive bone involvement affects most patients with myeloma, the predominant refractory plasma-cell malignancy.

basis: Cortisol elevation occurs in 3/4. In overt hypercortisolism, hypertension affects ~70%, skin atrophy/striae >50% and bone loss ~50%; subtype-specific frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypertension is a direct manifestation of cortisol excess in roughly 70% of overt cases; subtype-specific frequency is unavailable.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: sustained cortisol excess directly causes skin atrophy and striae in over 50% of overt cases; these are tissue changes rather than transient rash.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: cortisol directly causes bone loss in approximately 50% of overt cases; osteopenia, osteoporosis and kyphosis are supplied phenotypes.

basis: Open spinal neural-tube and vertebral defects; neurogenic bladder affects ~80-90% and neurogenic bowel ~70-90%, reflecting intrinsic loss of urinary and intestinal function.

decisions.renal: involved: neurogenic bladder affects approximately 80-90%, representing direct loss of bladder function from congenital spinal innervation damage.

basis: Scalp folds with defining neurodevelopmental abnormalities distinguish the non-essential form. Developmental cataracts occur in 30-79%; cardiac and skeletal defects are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: associated neurologic abnormalities distinguish the non-essential form; developmental impairment, seizures and structural brain injury are annotated at 30-79%.
